plan: Since this is the first round, I have no history to learn from. Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy in a second-price auction is to bid slightly below your true value. I will bid $48.9, which is just below my value of $49. This ensures I win if my value is the highest and pay the second highest bid.

I will employ a bidding strategy based on the Nash Equilibrium. With 3 bidders and values between 0 and 49, the optimal bid is approximately 2/3 of my value. In this round, my value is $44. Therefore, my bid should be around (2/3)*44 = 29.33. To be safe and account for the discrete bid increments, I will bid $29.3.

This is a single-round auction. The Nash Equilibrium for this type of auction is to bid slightly below your value. Since my value is $22, I will bid $21.9. This should give me a reasonable chance of winning while still securing a profit if I do win. I will avoid bidding my exact value or higher, as that would guarantee no profit or a loss.
